clue.text: Erratic don, past being able to change, wouldn't make decision

indicators.note: letters that are able to change can be rearranged, so the three words before are shuffled

explanation.surface: An unpredictable university lecturer, set in his ways, keeps putting off a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being able to change' is the anagram signal working on ERRATIC DON PAST; 'past being able to change' wants to describe the don's rigidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kept delaying and putting things off was failing to reach a decision.

clue.text: Big buildings around eastern district of London

indicators.note: around means the barns enclose the following letter

parts.note: barns are large farm buildings

explanation.surface: Large structures surround an eastern part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNES is a district of south-west London beside the Thames, not in the east despite 'eastern' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnes is a riverside area in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames.

clue.text: Adventure ceased sadly with the old man locked up inside

indicators.note: locked up inside means the father is shut within the rearranged letters
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of ceased are jumbled

parts.note: old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: An exploit came to an unhappy end once Dad was jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' gives ESCADE; 'locked up inside' shuts Dad within it, 'the old man' being familiar slang for a father.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure.

clue.text: Van booked to visit out-of-town areas?

definitions.text: Van booked to visit out-of-town areas?

parts.words: Van booked to visit out-of-town areas?
parts.note: booked reads as reserved, but the van is full of books touring rural villages

explanation.surface: A hired van is scheduled to call at rural places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' looks like reserved, but means stocked with books: a library on wheels touring villages.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling lending service in a vehicle visits villages lacking a permanent branch.

clue.text: Soldiers meeting fine author

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
well means fine, as in feeling fine

explanation.surface: Troops encounter a writer who levies penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm.

clue.text: Street artist having what could be seen as item of summer wear

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter in the road has something that might be summer clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater or panama woven from straw is headgear worn in warm weather.

clue.text: Touring group had so fallen apart in quarrel

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the quarrel

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: fallen apart means the letters of had so are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A travelling band had broken up after a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen apart' turns HAD SO into ADSHO, which goes 'in' ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring entertainment or promotional company moving from town to town.

clue.text: Occupant of No. 10 keeping repetitious performance for now

indicators.note: keeping means the leader holds the other piece inside

parts.note: the Prime Minister, PM, lives at 10 Downing Street
rote is mechanical repetition

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's monotonous act is merely temporary.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official residence; 'keeping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin pro tempore, shortened, means temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Decide to have lipstick etc — and no turning up with casual denims!

parts.note: lipstick and the like are make-up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reads the word no from bottom to top
casual suggests careless disorder, so denims is jumbled

explanation.surface: Wearing cosmetics but refusing scruffy jeans is a choice to be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes NO into ON; 'casual' rearranges DENIMS into ESMIND.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle on a choice after thought is to come to a resolution.

clue.text: Desperate news noted as it is broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of these words are spread and regathered

explanation.surface: Bulletin items are recorded as they air on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, not about the news going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely baffled and frantic is the state of utter desperation.

clue.text: Dance in African location given new ending

indicators.note: given new ending means the final letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Congo is a country in central Africa

explanation.surface: A dance in an African country gets a fresh finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given new ending' replaces the last O of CONGO with A.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance with a kick on every fourth beat.

clue.text: Lacking information as one suffering power cut?

definitions.meaning: uninformed, not told what is going on
literally without lights, sitting in blackness

explanation.surface: Someone sitting through a blackout knows nothing of what is happening.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept ignorant is figuratively being without light; a blackout makes it literal.

clue.text: A cop crossing street in danger?

indicators.note: crossing means the verb straddles the street abbreviation

parts.note: to cop is to take or catch

explanation.surface: A police officer walking over the road is at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a police officer but is the verb meaning catch or receive; 'crossing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at risk of being lost is endangered, like a wager laid down.

clue.text: An ugly drunk outside hotel, a wild beast

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters sit around the hotel letter
drunk suggests staggering disorder, so the letters of an ugly are jumbled

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An unattractive inebriate outside a hotel behaves like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges AN UGLY into NYLGAU, set 'outside' H.
explanation.definitionFit: The nylghau, or nilgai, is a large Indian antelope.

clue.text: Absent-minded performance that results from a baddy getting needled?

definitions.meaning: idle drumming of fingers on a table without thinking

definitions.text: results from a baddy getting needled
definitions.meaning: the arch-villain being inked by a needle would get a body marking

explanation.surface: A distracted act is what a villain gets when pricked with needles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needled' means irritated in the surface but here means inked by a tattooist.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless finger drumming is traditionally called by this name; read literally it is Satan's body art.

clue.text: Judge has landed property — this writer's entertained

indicators.note: entertained means the estate hosts the setter's contraction inside it

parts.note: an estate is a large holding of land
this writer is the setter, so this writer's is I'm, I am

explanation.surface: A magistrate owns land where the writer is a guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun for the magistrate but is the verb; 'entertained' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to make an approximate assessment of it.

clue.text: Sanctions a very quiet ramble first thing on Sunday

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
to rove is to wander or ramble

indicators.note: first thing on means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone authorises a peaceful stroll early on Sunday morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first thing on' takes S from Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or endorse it officially.

clue.text: More insane knight, say, going around India

parts.note: N is knight in chess notation

indicators.note: going around means the verb encircles the India letter

parts.note: to say is to utter
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A madder knight speaks while touring India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' puts I inside UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is informal for crazy, so the comparative means crazier.

clue.text: Boxed, so as to be safe

definitions.meaning: packed inside a container or casing
as a precaution, should something happen

explanation.surface: Packed away for security.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally inside a container, and idiomatically as a precaution.

clue.text: Troublemaker meets fools — shortly there's deadlock

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: shortly means the word for fools is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: asses are fools

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker meets idiots and soon nothing moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final S of ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate where no progress is possible is a standstill.

clue.text: Rock mostly split over time

indicators.note: mostly means the word for split loses its last letter

parts.note: a schism is a split or division

explanation.surface: A boulder has largely cracked over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops M from SCHISM; in a down clue 'over' puts SCHIS above T.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic stone that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: Folk may naughtily process them for absent colleagues — scam tried out

definitions.text: Folk may naughtily process them for absent colleagues

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, so scam tried is rearranged

explanation.surface: Clocking in for missing workmates is a fraud that has been attempted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SCAM TRIED; the definition describes clocking in on behalf of a colleague who is not there.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers stamp attendance records at a clock, and a dishonest friend might punch them for an absentee.

clue.text: Old characters journey back to meet flood survivor

indicators.note: back means the word for journey is read in reverse

parts.note: to go is to journey
Ham was a son of Noah who survived the Flood in the ark

explanation.surface: Ancient figures travel home to meet someone who escaped a deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses GO to OG.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an early Irish alphabet of strokes carved on stone.

clue.text: Journalist about to face ordeal with hate being shown

indicators.note: about means the journalist abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a test can be a trying ordeal

explanation.surface: A reporter is about to undergo a trial while loathing is evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is to abhor it.

clue.text: Not all islanders enjoy writer of fairy stories

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some island people like a teller of fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen, the Danish storyteller, wrote The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling.
